news.title: 'I wanted to win another World Cup, I coudn't': Lionel Messi pens emotional post after father's demise
news.lede: For the first time since the death of his father Jorge Messi earlier this month, Lionel Messi has spoken publicly, sharing an emotional tribute that offered a deeply personal look at the grief he has been carrying throughout one of the most difficult periods of his life. The Argentina captain posted a photograph with his father alongside the simple caption, "Te amo, pa" ("I love you, Dad"), before accompanying it with a heartfelt letter reflecting on their relationship, the 2026 FIFA World Cup, and the uncertainty he now feels about life without the man who had been beside him since the very beginning." Dad, I still can't believe you're gone"Messi began by admitting that he is still struggling to accept his father's passing." Dad, I still can't believe you're gone.

news.title: Messi unsure he will play 'much longer' after father's death
news.lede: Jorge Messi watched his son Lionel Messi lead Argentina to victory at the 2022 World Cup. Lionel Messi said he is unsure how much longer he will continue playing football as he posted an emotional tribute after his father's death. Messi's father Jorge was 68 when he died last week following a long illness. Jorge had been the Argentina forward's agent since he was 14 and watched him become one of the sport's greatest ever players.

news.title: Roberto Martinez 'in talks to become new Netherlands boss' despite World Cup failures with Portugal and Belgium
news.lede: ROBERTO MARTINEZ has held talks over the vacant Netherlands national team job. The former Premier League boss, 53, is available after leaving Portugal following their World Cup exit. Dutch football chiefs are after a new boss as they look to replace Ronald Koeman, who departed after his men lost to Morocco on penalties in the round of 32. According to De Telegraaf, Dutch technical director Nigel de Jong has spoken to Martinez regarding the role.

news.title: Manchester United: Youri Tielemans on his dream move, injuries and playing with Marcus Rashford
news.lede: Youri Tielemans has 90 caps for Belgium and played in the 2026 World Cup. It was third time lucky this summer in the history of Youri Tielemans and Manchester United. United looked seriously at the Belgium midfielder in 2019, after Tielemans had impressed in an initial loan spell at Leicester. And again in 2022, as they spent too long holding out for Frenkie de Jong to decide if he was prepared to leave Barcelona.

news.title: WAFCON 2026 Semi-finals: World Cup berths secured, final places at stake
news.lede: The semi-final line-up for WAFCON 2026 sees Morocco, Cameroon, Algeria, and Malawi battle for places in the final after securing qualification for the 2027 FIFA Women’s World Cup. Their quarter-final victories not only kept their title ambitions alive but also confirmed their places among Africa’s representatives in Brazil next year. Morocco have continued their impressive rise on the continental stage, reaching the semi-finals for a third consecutive edition and remaining unbeaten. The Atlas Lionesses, coached by Jorge Vilda, remain in pursuit of a maiden WAFCON title after overcoming South Africa, the side that beat them in the 2022 final.

news.title: Gianni Infantino eyes another huge World Cup change to secure position as FIFA chief
news.lede: FIFA President Gianni Infantino has reportedly expressed a willingness to support another expansion of the World Cup. It has been suggested that Infantino would be in favour of the tournament increasing from 48 to 64 teams, amid ongoing uncertainty around his future in the job. The uncertainty followed news which emerged that FIFA had proposals that would have seen them sell shares of the federation’s tournaments to private investors. The controversial scheme would have affected the men's and women's World Cups, as well as the Club World Cup, but was shelved following a substantial backlash.

news.title: Messi says he is unsure he will play 'for much longer' after father's death
news.lede: Lionel Messi has paid an emotional tribute to his late father Jorge, who died aged 68 last week, saying he is "not sure I'll carry on" playing football.

news.title: Argentina star Messi not certain to play “much longer” after father’s death
news.lede: Former Barcelona and PSG star Lionel Messi, who won the 2022 World Cup, hints at retirement from football.
